result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.clique_number()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the clique number (size of the maximum clique). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12365-L12463){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.clique_number() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Clique number](/assets/graphs/clique-number.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node graph whose largest cliques have three nodes. One of them, A B C, is drawn in the accent color; B C D ties it, and no four nodes are all linked. The card gives the clique number 3." width="100%"} The clique number `ω(G)` is the size of the largest clique in the graph. This is a fundamental graph invariant used in graph theory and combinatorial optimization. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Size of the maximum clique. Returns `0` for empty graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The clique number $\omega(G)$ is one of the fundamental graph invariants and is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard to compute in general. Extremes are easy to reason about, though: for the complete graph $\omega(K_n) = n$; for any bipartite graph $\omega(G) \le 2$, because a third vertex would need to be adjacent to two already-adjacent vertices, contradicting bipartiteness; and for any triangle-free graph the same $\omega(G) \le 2$ bound holds. The implementation shares the Bron-Kerbosch enumeration behind `find_cliques()` and inherits its $O(3^{n/3})$ worst-case bound. Undirected graphs only. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6b1b2afe .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A path's largest clique is just a single edge, since no three nodes form a triangle: ::: {#e1c63da0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: An empty graph has clique number `0`: ::: {#c3c85ba1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph(directed=False).clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph `K_n` always has clique number `n`: ::: {#f3bdb95e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=7) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 7 ``` ::: ::: Bipartite graphs can never contain a triangle, so their clique number never exceeds `2`: ::: {#ce4aaa85 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("A", "D") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("B", "D") ) graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
